fi-brachygobius-doriae.title: Bumblebee Goby
fi-brachygobius-doriae.summary: The bumblebee goby, Brachygobius doriae, is a small goby from western Borneo and the Natuna Islands, described from Sarawak. Among the more frequently traded members of the genus, it is often…
rows: Omnivore. Small live foods such as Artemia, Daphnia, etc., should be considered essential although some specimens will learn to accept frozen alternatives.
Described from the Malaysian state of Sarawak on the island of Borneo, and appears endemic to western parts of the island plus the Natuna Islands archipelago which lies off…
notes: Provide plenty of hiding places and cover, the idea being to create broken lines of sight to allow weaker individuals to escape continual attention from dominant fish.
Crushed coral or coral sand can be mixed into the substrate to act as a buffer if necessary, or marine salt added at a dose of around 2 grams per litre.

fi-stiphodon-atropurpureus.title: Stiphodon atropurpureus
fi-stiphodon-atropurpureus.summary: The blue neon goby, Stiphodon atropurpureus, is a stream-dwelling goby from southern Japan, Taiwan, southern China, the Philippines and Malaysia. It is available occasionally but often under the…
rows: The type specimens were collected from Rizal Province, Luzon Island, and Lanao del Norte Province, Mindanao Island, the Philippines.
notes: These gobies aren't too difficult to keep provided some basic requirements are met.
Most importantly the water must be clean and well-oxygenated at all times so we suggest the use of either an over-sized filter, additional powerheads, flow pumps, or airstones.

fi-tateurndina-ocellicauda.title: Peacock Gudgeon Florida
fi-tateurndina-ocellicauda.summary: The peacock goby, Tateurndina ocellicauda, is a small sleeper from Papua New Guinea, found in lowland rainforest streams, ponds and rivers. The name is misleading, as it belongs to the Eleotridae,…
rows: Omnivore. Will usually accept dried food but much prefers small live and frozen stuff, such as bloodworm, daphnia, brineshrimp etc.
notes: This species prefers soft, slightly acidic water and lots of cover.
The use of a dark substrate and floating vegetation will help it feel more secure and show its best colouration.

fi-neovespicula-depressifrons.title: Indian Butterfly Goby (Leaf Goblinfish)
fi-neovespicula-depressifrons.summary: Not a true goby: a small, leaf-like waspfish with a huge dorsal fin, from brackish coasts of Indonesia, New Guinea and the Philippines. Delicate, and its spines are venomous.
rows: Peaceful but delicate; avoid boisterous or fin-nipping fish such as puffers
Frozen foods: brine shrimp, mysis, bloodworm and mosquito larvae
Indonesia, New Guinea and the Philippines
notes: Soft sand and plenty of hiding places suit it.
warn: Venom glands at the base of some spines: take care when netting and during maintenance.

fi-stiphodon-semoni.title: Cobalt Blue Goby (Stiphodon semoni)
fi-stiphodon-semoni.summary: A small stream goby from Indonesia to New Guinea and the Solomon Islands. Males carry a bright metallic blue stripe. It grazes algae and biofilm off rocks and needs clean, oxygen-rich water.
rows: About 2 in (50 mm) SL (Seriously Fish); FishBase lists 4.6 cm SL
Peaceful; pick calm, similar-sized stream fish or dwarf shrimp as tankmates
Specialised algae grazer: needs rocks with a natural growth of algae and biofilm (strong lighting helps). Sinking dried and small meaty foods may be taken but should be offered only now and then
Western Sumatra east across Indonesia to northern New Guinea and the Solomon Islands (described from Ambon)
notes: Use an oversized filter or extra powerheads/airstones; strong oxygenation matters more than torrent-like flow.
Often sold under the wrong name (e.g. S. elegans or S. atropurpureus).
